_about.names: emName (core_common msg, LMD) at index = the monster number = the em number, the index the MH4U Hunting Log reads quest monsters by. Where emName repeats the base monster's name (Apex, Savage, Furious, Rusted ...) the name is the Hunting Log's VARIANTS one and nameSource says so; nameRom keeps the game's word.
_about.model: the body model the monster's own archive packs; sharesModelOf names its folder when it is another monster's. lists: every motion list the archive packs, `shared` when it is another monster's file (same bytes).
_about.textures: the New 3DS (romfs/snake) copies where the game ships them, else the standard ones; texFrom counts which
_about.hideIdx: mesh-table +0 bit 0 clear (the MHGU and MH3U draw-mask field); the 4U draw code that tests it has not been read.
_about.species: HAND-KEPT, not read from the game: no Monster List table has been found in 4U's code (3U's is). The species names and their order are the game's own -- HunterNote 22-35, the Hunter's Notes type line, and 20 ("???") for Gore Magala -- but which monster has which is the MH4U Quest Randomizer's hand-kept MONSTER_CLASS for the large monsters and this app's scripts/species.py for the small ones. `small` is hand-kept the same way; `speciesFrom` is "hand" on every row so nothing passes for ROM data.
_about.sizeBase: 1.0: the monster size tables are not decoded for 4U.
_about.partTable: the monster's emd parts rows (em_data.arc enemy\emNNN\data\emNNN, type 0x0a0e48d4; parts4u.py), from its own emd else its model folder's (`partsFrom`), as [part, group, cond, mode, param, threshold] with group 255 on every row (4U rows have no group). Conds are read as 3U's (mh3u_parts.py); 4U's own reader is not traced, and conds 10 and 11 are new in 4U and not decoded. MODES: every 4U row counts (inferred: 229 parts carry 2+ rows, dead under 3U's first-row rule), so 4U mode 0 ships as 2 (hidden while c) and mode 1 as 3 (hidden while not c). A severed piece is tied to its cut bit by `cutBit` (bit 1 for a tail, the 3U convention); a piece with none is a prop. null: no emd rows (the page then hides the pieces and only opens the eyes).
_about.boneNodes: every bone node of the model as [three.js name, global bone id, is a _s leaf].

_about.retargeted: a list whose `retargeted` is set plays from a copy of `source` with that many bone nodes renamed by global bone id to the monster's own model: the monster borrows the list from a skeleton with the same bones in another order, and the viewer binds tracks by node name.
_about.eyesClosedParts: the body parts drawn only while the eyes are closed -- the parts whose first row in the monster's emd parts table (em_data.arc, parts4u.py; `eyesFrom` names whose) is cond 0 (eyes closed) with mode 1. The viewer hides them, so every monster's eyes are open; the rest of the table is not applied yet. Monsters with no eyelids (Khezu, Gore Magala, the Seltas, Nerscylla, Zamtrios) have none.
_about.apex: an Apex is a state of its base monster, not an entry: {id, name, lists}. Its archive packs the base's model, materials, textures and parts rows byte for byte; the page's Apex switch plays `lists` (every list the Apex archive packs: the base's, plus Apex Rajang's and Apex Diablos' list 4; Apex Zinogre's three are Zinogre's, byte for byte, under its own name) and turns on cond 10, the Frenzy state (the Virus layer and angry eyes), with the effect layers. That cond 10 is the Apex look is inferred: no Apex data sets it. The Apex particle effects (efl) are not drawn.
